title: Conditions of Carriage: Cancelling a Ticket for a Crestline Flight Credit
content:
**Article on voluntary cancellation — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** A customer may cancel a ticket that is ticketed or partially flown and keep its unused value as a Crestline Flight Credit in the passenger's name when the fare brand permits cancellation for credit.

## 1. Timing

A cancellation for credit must be confirmed no later than the scheduled departure of the first unflown flight minus the fare brand's cancellation cutoff hours. The cutoff is counted back in full elapsed hours from the first unflown departure recorded on the ticket, and a cancellation confirmed exactly at the cutoff is still accepted; after it the ticket is handled as a no-show.

| First unflown departure 10:00, 1-hour cutoff (hypothetical) | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Cancellation confirmed at 09:00 | Accepted |
| Cancellation confirmed at 09:01 | Past the cutoff; handled as a no-show |

## 2. Cancellation fee and credit amount

2.1 The cancellation fee is the fare brand's domestic, short-haul international or long-haul international cancellation fee according to the ticket's itinerary class. It is retained from the ticket value as a forfeiture entry whose ground is the cancellation fee; a fee of zero is not recorded.

2.2 The credit amount is the residual value less the cancellation fee. When the fee equals or exceeds the residual value, the whole residual is retained as the fee and no credit is issued.

2.3 The credit-conversion entry moves the net value out of the ticket, and a Crestline Flight Credit is issued for exactly that amount; the credit's validity and use then follow the flight credit terms.

| Hypothetical Crestline Basic Economy ticket | Residual value | Fee | Credit issued |
|---|---|---|---|
| Domestic | 240.00 | 99 | 141.00 |
| Short-haul international | 149.00 | 149 | None (whole residual retained) |
| Long-haul international | 120.00 | 199 | None (120.00 retained as the fee) |

## 3. Records and eligibility of the conversion

- A credit conversion is booked only on a ticket whose status is cancelled to credit.
- A credit conversion is made only for a ticket whose recorded form of payment is credit card, debit card, flight credit or corporate invoice. An award ticket is cancelled through the Summit award redeposit rule, and a companion ticket through the companion reinstatement rule.

## 4. Fees and refundable brands

Seat, bag, change and upgrade fees are not refunded on a voluntary cancellation for credit and are never added to the credit. A refundable fare brand may be cancelled for credit only when the customer chooses a credit over the refund.
